summary: Burst p95/p99 latency after continuous-batcher occupancy resets on Dedicated cluster
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaDocs (Dedicated) reports recurring p95/p99 latency bursts and intermittent 504s starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Problem correlates with periods of low sustained QPS followed by short spikes.

Impact:
- Multiple API requests from NovaDocs observed hitting >3s p95 and >8s p99 during bursts; some 504 timeouts recorded.
- Affects production inference for their core document-summarization feature; customer reported user-visible slowdowns and error rates increasing ~1.6%.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: dc-west-3 (us-west region)
- Serving runtime v1.16.4; continuous-batcher v2.3.1
- Traffic pattern: baseline 2 rps per tenant with periodic microbursts to ~30 rps

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Warm the model with low steady traffic (~2 rps) for 10–15 minutes.
2) Trigger a short high-concurrency run (~30 rps for 30s).
3) Observe p95/p99 on requests that arrive in the 30–120s window after the burst.

Observed logs/metrics:
- Grafana panels show batcher occupancy reset events aligning with p99 spikes (panels: batcher/occupancy, batcher/flush-latency, request/timeout-rate).
- Sample log excerpt from serving pod (pod-id: sr-73a9): "coalescer: occupancy reset due to tenant-shard-reassign; linger amplified to 120ms" followed by "flush_delay: 380ms" and subsequent 504s.
- Traces show many requests entering the coalescer queue, then a long linger followed by a single large flush containing short and long sequences together, increasing GPU kernel overhead and KV cache misses.

Customer notes:
- The customer pins model version and cannot tolerate repeated long-tail latency. They requested an interim mitigation and ETA for a permanent fix.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Triage: Support confirmed customer traces and requested SRE engagement.
2026-03-10 11:10 UTC - SRE replicated pattern in staging by replaying NovaDocs traffic profile; observed occupancy reset when shard reweighting job ran (cron: tenant-reshard).

Hypothesis A: Resharding/occupancy reset causes batcher linger timers to reinitialize incorrectly -> temporary increase in linger + larger coalesced batches that mix short/long sequences -> p99 amplification.
Hypothesis B: After reset, KV cache associations are invalidated for a small window, increasing per-token compute and causing downstream queuing/backpressure.

Metric snapshots collected: batcher/occupancy_histogram, flush_size_distribution, kv-cache/miss-rate, pipeline/queue-length (links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/nb2k-batcher/batcher-overview?orgId=1&var-cluster=dc-west-3).
Reproduced in staging w/ tenant-reshard enabled; correlation high between reshard event and 30–90s post-event p99 elevation.
Logs: observed coalescer debug messages with linger being set to default 120ms after occupancy reset; previously tuned linger had been 8ms for this tenant (per dedicated-config).
Checked recent deploys: no serving runtime change in last 7 days; scheduler rebalancer job config updated 2026-03-09 (PR #7890) to improve shard balance—likely root trigger.
Related incidents: SUP-17012 shows similar long-tail behavior during batcher transitions; linked for context.
Customer-provided payload shapes: mixture of short (<20 tokens) and long (>600 tokens) requests increases kernel-switch overhead when coalesced.
Temporary reproduction script added to internal repo: tools/repro/tenant_reshard_burst_profile.py (used in staging)
comments: Support (Priya): 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Acknowledged. Engaging SRE to validate logs and staging replay. First response sent to customer with request for timeframe and sample request IDs.

SRE (Marco): 2026-03-10 12:20 UTC - Confirmed correlation with tenant-reshard. Staging replay reproduced p99 spikes. Hypothesize occupancy reset resets linger to default; creating INT ticket for scheduler team.
Customer (NovaDocs - Sarah Liao): 2026-03-10 13:05 UTC - Thanks for the quick triage. Can you confirm whether we should expect more incidents? We need a short-term mitigation.

Support (Priya): 2026-03-10 13:30 UTC - Provided workaround: disable scheduled tenant-reshard on their dedicated cluster (we can gate the job per-customer) and enabled tenant-specific continuous-batcher override to keep linger at 8ms during rebalancing window. Customer asked SRE to apply the override.

SRE (Marco): 2026-03-11 08:45 UTC - Applied per-tenant linger override and paused reshard cron on dc-west-3 for NovaDocs. Initial metrics show p99 returning to baseline within 20 minutes. Observed KV-miss rate drop and smaller flush sizes.
Support (Priya): 2026-03-11 10:00 UTC - Notified customer of temporary mitigation and proposed timeline for permanent fix (see resolution).
resolution:
Workaround applied: paused scheduler tenant-reshard cron for affected cluster and added per-tenant continuous-batcher linger override to preserve tuned linger during rebalances.
Permanent fix plan: engineering to modify resharding sequence so occupancy metadata is preserved across shard moves, and ensure continuous-batcher maintains effective linger and KV-cache bindings across reshard events. Patch PR created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/7941).
Rollout notes: patch targets scheduler v3.4.2; will deploy to staging and run customer traffic replay for 48h before canary to dc-west-3. Expected ETA for canary: 2026-03-19; full rollout 2026-03-24 pending validation.
Follow-ups: create automated test to simulate reshard-induced occupancy resets (owner: serving-runtime team), add alert when batcher linger diverges from per-tenant overrides, and add postmortem after full rollout.

Applied per-tenant continuous-batcher linger override (8ms) - 2026-03-11 08:40 UTC
Created INT ticket for scheduler team: INT-442
Opened scheduler PR to preserve occupancy metadata during reweights: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/7941
notes_for_customer_success: Customer notified of mitigation and agreed to temporary pause of resharding. Recommend SRE keep pause until canary completes; CS will coordinate billing/ops impact if any. Ensure runbook updated with per-tenant override steps.
